title: jerlov: inherent optical properties of the Jerlov optical water types, with provenance
description:
Absorption and scattering coefficients for the Jerlov optical water types, taken from the primary literature with the provenance of every value recorded.

Values that a published table got wrong are flagged rather than silently repaired, and quantities the data do not determine are refused rather than guessed. Thirty-five entries are documented, thirteen of them confirmed defects in the source literature: duplicated rows in Solonenko & Mobley (2015) Table 7, a transcription error in the small-particle scattering coefficient that propagated into their published coefficients, a Data Availability Statement that gives the DOI of an unrelated dataset, a reprint whose stated unit is out by a factor of ten, a misprinted equation for trichromatic colour thresholds in Vorobyev & Osorio (1998), a row of Smith & Baker (1981) Table I whose pure water absorption exceeds its own diffuse attenuation, a sign misprinted in Duntley's (1963) equation for the apparent radiance along a slanted line of sight, and a second factor of one half printed inside Fresnel's law in Gregg & Carder (1990). Three further entries were open questions that obtaining the 1968 first edition settled. The same Jerlov water type is in circulation with beam attenuations differing by a factor of five, which is why every coefficient here carries the source it came from.

Every shipped table can be regenerated from its primary source by the scripts in tools/, and each generation step checks the result against the equations of the paper it came from.

The package computes the direct and veiling components along a horizontal underwater path, or a slanted one in uniform water (Duntley 1963), converts spectra to CIE XYZ, sRGB, or the response of an arbitrary camera or set of photoreceptors, gives the Jerlov type that typically applies in each 10 m layer down to 200 m and carries the downwelling irradiance down through those layers, integrates photosynthetically available radiation (PAR), or the photon flux over any other band or weighted by any spectral sensitivity, with depth, gives the spectrum at any depth and the effective Kd between two, and finds the depth at which PAR falls to 1 percent, ranks the Jerlov types by their distance from a measured Kd spectrum, carries Jerlov's measured profiles of quanta irradiance (350-700 nm) by water type and checks the depth profile against them, carries Tyler's (1958) measured radiance distribution in Lake Pend Oreille, carries the wave-induced light fluctuations measured by Darecki et al. (2011) and Gernez & Antoine (2009), read from their figures, carries the Paulson & Simpson (1977) shortwave penetration parameters used by ocean circulation models, converts a backscattering sensor's single-angle reading into the backscattering coefficient, carries Petzold's (1972) volume scattering functions for eight measured ocean waters, gives the absorbance template of a visual pigment of Govardovskii et al. (2000) for a peak wavelength and chromophore the caller states, and gives the distance between two colours in units of receptor noise by the model of Vorobyev & Osorio (1998), for a noise the caller states. Without a water type, it gives Kd from the chlorophyll concentration of case 1 water (Morel & Maritorena 2001) or from the absorption and backscattering coefficients and the sun (Lee et al. 2005, 2013), the remote sensing reflectance from a and bb (Gordon et al. 1988; Lee et al. 2002), and the Secchi depth from Kd and that reflectance (Lee et al. 2015), and inverts the reflectance to the absorption and backscattering coefficients by the quasi-analytical algorithm, in the version of IOCCG Report 5 (2006), checked against that report's published statistics, and as QAA_v6, checked against its author's spreadsheet. It carries four published spectra of the absorption of pure water, Pope & Fry (1997), Smith & Baker (1981), Mason, Cone & Fry (2016) and Lee et al. (2015), for the caller to choose from, and removes Raman scattering from a measured reflectance by the empirical correction of Lee et al. (2013). From chlorophyll it gives the absorption by phytoplankton (Bricaud et al. 1995) and the backscattering by particles (Morel & Maritorena 2001) of case 1 water, and the reflectance with molecular and particle backscattering kept apart, for the seven viewing geometries of Lee et al. (2011). It gives the downwelling distribution function D0 from the sun and the share of direct sunlight, and rescales a Kd to another light field by Kd/D0 (Gordon 1989). It gives the direct and diffuse irradiance just above and just below the sea surface under a cloudless sky, at every nm from 350 to 700, by the model of Gregg & Carder (1990), with its table of the sun's spectrum and the gases' absorption transcribed and every input describing the atmosphere left to the caller.
